_notes_fit_out: Fit Out Your Ship (docs/fit-out-contract.md; design page docs/mockups/loadout; read into GameData.FitOut by game/sim/Data/GameData.FitOut.cs, rules in game/sim/Core/FitOut.cs). Before leaving home the player picks a focus, splits the ship's crew over the divisions and loads the hold. Optional: without this file no ship is fitted out and the menu skips the page; a game started without a fit-out (tests, the sandbox, the balance runner, the ships not listed under ships) plays exactly as before. All numbers are placeholders. rules: crew_floor_share = the least share of the crew every division holds (rounded up to whole heads); focus_floor_share = the least share of the focus's own division; effect_per_point = a division's strength per percentage point its crew share is above or below an even split (100 / the number of divisions = 25): strength = effect_per_point x (share in percent - 25); replaces_start_stock = the resources of surfaces landing.start_stock that a fit-out replaces with what its cargo gives (every other start-stock resource stays, and the ship's own start_bonus / start_units are added as always). divisions (the order of a fit-out's crew list): id, name, who (the people in it). focuses: id, name, division (its own division, null for the all-rounder), line (one short sentence), crew_pct (the preset's shares in division order, summing to 100; rounded to heads by largest remainder, never below a floor), perk (the text shown; empty = none), perk_levers (lever id: a multiplier the focus puts on that lever), landing_reveal (hexes revealed round the hub at the landing instead of surfaces landing.reveal_radius; leave out for no change). levers (the numbers a fit-out moves; the sim multiplies each where gravity, weather or research already do): id, division (the division whose strength moves it, or null for a lever only perks and cargo move), more_is_better (true: x (1 + strength); false: x (1 - strength)), name (for the summary). The lever ids are fixed by the sim: drive_speed (ground vehicle speed), satellite_sweep (seconds a survey satellite takes round its band), drone_battery (scout drone battery seconds), rover_hazard (rover hazard and flat-tyre chance), build_time (building and upgrade time), repair_speed (repairs and maintenance), fabrication (Machine Shop and hub workshop speed), wear (building wear), research_rate (Research Lab points), dig_time (excavation seconds a layer), sickness (seconds a pathogen find keeps a base's crew sick), wildlife (wildlife attacks on vehicles a minute), ruin_defence (damage of a woken ruin defence), crew_loss (crew lost a minute when life support fails); without a division: hazard_damage (damage a rover takes from a hazard), wildlife_damage (from a wildlife attack), ruin_vehicle_damage (a vehicle's share of a ruin defence's damage), hub_workshop (the hub workshop's speed, on top of fabrication), mission_research (research points from missions). cargo_groups: id (a division id or ship), name, floor (containers the group must hold). cargo (the lines, in page order): id, name, group, containers (hold space each), min / max (how many may be loaded), text (what one gives, shown on hover), and what one does: stock (resource: amount into the landing stock), unit (a surface unit that lands with the colony, in a convoy drop ship like a ship's start_units), satellites (survey satellites that launch without paying their cost), research (points banked toward the first tech researched), levers (lever id: added to that lever's multiplier per item, so -0.08 x 3 items = x 0.76). ships (only the ships listed are fitted out; phase 1 = the two colony ships): ship (a ship_choice.json id that colonizes), crew (heads to assign), hold (containers), suggest (the focus the page starts on, and the preset that replaces a fit-out the rules refuse), base (cargo every preset starts from; it must meet every line minimum and group floor), fill (per focus: the lines added one at a time, in this order, round and round, while the line is under its max and the hold has room). Checked by Validate(): ids, floors and budgets, and every focus's preset legal on every listed ship.
